prompt:
A densely annotated editorial infographic plate, drawn by hand in confident ink
line with light watercolour and gouache wash on bright warm-white paper.
Contour line varies in weight and is charcoal near-black. Dimensional but not
photographic: restrained hatching, subtle texture, believable volume, selective
shadow, clean uncluttered background. Every material reads as itself — dull grey
lead, unglazed earthenware, weathered timber, damp fibrous bark — and materials
that differ in the explanation look visibly different. Quiet palette of stone,
clay, wood, and metal tones over the warm-white ground, with one or two
desaturated accents that each keep a single meaning throughout the plate.
Contemporary editorial typography: one calm display face for the title, one
highly legible face for the many small labels, sentence case, crisply printed
and correctly spelled. Annotation is dense and disciplined — leader lines,
brackets, dimension marks, magnified inset circles, small side studies — laid
out so no two leaders cross. Asymmetric composition with about a quarter of the
page left quiet. Modern printing on clean stock: fresh, crisp, and unaged. The
only lettering anywhere on the plate is the title, the deck, the labels, and the
short notes. The words hero, drawing, figure, plate, inset, zone, band, strip,
trio, column, and cutaway describe the construction of the page and are never
lettered onto it, alone or in a phrase: no headings that name parts of the
layout, no percentages or
proportions of the page, no tags in brackets after a label or note, no sentence
describing the drawing or explaining what the reader is meant to see, no
signature, monogram, date, watermark, or credit line.

The plate is headed "colorize", with the standing line "Walks every engraving in a book's image ledger through one chosen colouring method, carrying the ledger onward for later stages." beneath it.

The dominant picture, filling roughly half the page, shows On the left sits an open ledger listing images. Beside it is a stack of black-and-white engravings cut from book pages. The engravings travel rightward along a track to a five-way junction dial with exits named copy, ai, sepia, deoldify and python-script. The ai exit splits into four parallel lanes, each carrying one engraving to an image model. One engraving drops off a lane marked failed and set aside, while the other lanes keep moving. On the far right, the engravings emerge as softly coloured prints.

Magnified circles set beside it show The first circle shows an engraving flagged no_sky whose top stays unblued. The second shows a tall engraving matched to the nearest of nine allowed shapes, so its caption is not cropped. The third shows one returned print named JPEG and another named PNG, each labelled for what came back. The small studies show the same engraving five ways: unchanged, sepia-toned, colourised by the AI, by DeOldify, and by a custom script.

Colour is used so that Warm ochre marks colour being added to an image. Muted red marks a failed image that was skipped. Slate blue marks the ledger and its copy travelling with the images.

Draw these quantities as dimension marks or counts: 5 colouring methods at the junction; 4 parallel workers by default on the ai lanes; 9 allowed shapes in the aspect circle; 1 ledger in and 1 ledger out; 2 model tiers, cheap and pro, beside the image model.

These trade words appear on the plate, each set against the thing it names: manifest.yaml sits on the ledger at the start and again in the output group. --tool sits on the junction dial. copy, ai, sepia, deoldify and python-script sit on its five exits. --workers sits on the four parallel lanes. no_sky sits on the flagged engraving. --copy-to sits on the arrow to the second folder. cheap and pro sit beside the image model. JPEG and PNG sit on the returned prints.

Letter these words onto the drawings, spelled exactly as given: manifest.yaml, cut engravings, --tool, copy, ai, sepia, deoldify, python-script, --workers, image model, failed, skipped. no_sky, no blue sky, nearest aspect, JPEG from Gemini, PNG from OpenAI. copied through, sepia tone, Impressionist palette, if installed, your own script. colored images, manifest copied, --copy-to, second folder. chosen folder, supporting folder, colorize folder, rerun fills gaps.

Set these short notes beside what they explain: Default copy passes originals through uncoloured; A failed image never stops the run. Flagged images keep their tops sky-free; Matched shape keeps captioned plates uncropped; File named for the bytes returned. Same engraving, five treatments side by side. Ledger travels on for downstream stages; Mirror copy made in the same pass. Output folder chosen in this order.
